findings: November product matrix changes Checkout and Express Checkout Element from unsupported to supported, with private preview explicitly attached to Express Checkout Element only. Express Checkout Element has new substantive prose for custom buttons alongside Apple Pay/Google Pay, plus an implementation link. Payment Links remains unsupported, while Connect, Payment Element, Mobile Payment Element, Subscriptions, Invoicing and Customer Portal remain supported.

Dashboard creates branded types, November guides users to presets for Payment Element and custom branding for a custom frontend or Payment Methods API. The type ID is stored by the merchant and cannot be retrieved through the API, while custom PaymentMethod instances can be created and retrieved with type custom and the Dashboard cpmt_ ID in custom[type].

Transaction authorization and processing stay with the merchant and third-party PSP, including charges, refunds, disputes, settlement and completion/reconciliation after selection. Stripe can optionally receive Payment Records for reporting and manage Billing subscription state and tracking of external payments; a record is not Stripe processing.

Connect platform can create the method in a connected account with its own or the connected account’s type. May’s Node stripeAccount option and November’s cURL Stripe-Account header both express connected-account request scope. Existing source describes the option itself as a header.

Both dates require the merchant to maintain its own direct PSP integration and active PSP agreement. The PSP operates the service. An ended PSP agreement or Stripe notifying or documenting a prohibition requires immediate CPM removal and PSP integration disablement. Where Stripe removes or blocks access and gives notice, ignoring required removal means the CPM does not render. Marks and local crypto restrictions are retained.
November reorganizes setup, headings and JSON formatting and swaps Node for cURL. These presentational changes preserve the PaymentMethod creation and Connect account scope.
substantive_changes: Checkout now marked supported at product level in the November matrix; Express Checkout Element changes to private preview and has custom-button display guidance. Do not extend these labels to hosted UI details, preview requirements or live processing behavior absent evidence.
historical_claims_to_preserve: May 8, 2026 marks Checkout and Express Checkout Element unsupported and lists more than 50 external payment-method presets. Retain the dated baseline alongside November evidence.

Both dates distinguish Dashboard types and API-created method objects, preserve optional external reporting and Connect account scope, and leave payment and downstream disputes/refunds/settlement with the external payment chain.
May quantified over 50 presets. November gives branding guidance without a catalog count. Neither a current count nor a catalog change follows from this wording difference.
